summary: Pend Oreille County DNR lookout: 30-ft L-4 tower built 1945, 40-ft DNR cab 1962, destroyed 1986; footings in photo captions; old access road crosses private land.

facts.design: 30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab (1945); 40-foot wooden DNR live-in cab (1962)
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1986 (the Weebly page says toppled). Willhite photo captions mention footings and a benchmark; none of those captions is dated.

access.note: The DNR owns the very top of the mountain, but the old access road is on private property, per the Willhite page

visit.trail_note: Willhite gives a hike of 1.3 miles with 800 feet of elevation gain; nothing stands to climb now.

events.note: Short-wave radio installed at the lookout site in June 1944; structure then unknown
Charles Heppe, a veteran firefighter, was the lookout
30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab; Spokane newspaper reported it complete in August 1945 with Heppe in charge
Laura Belle Johnson listed as lookout 1957-1962
First tower replaced by a 40-foot wooden DNR live-in cab, built by the Department's own carpentry crew at around $8,000
Destroyed per FireLookout.com and Willhite; Weebly says toppled
Registered December 17, 2012 as US 1523, WA 423; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FireLookout.com and the Willhite page say the tower was destroyed in 1986, and the Weebly page says toppled that year. Both describe the same loss, so the story reports the 1986 event once with both words.

notes_for_editor: Brief height 12.2 m (40 ft) describes the 1962 cab only; the 1945 tower was 30 ft (about 9.1 m), so the story gives both. Brief agency and coordinates match the FFLOS record. Willhite photo captions (footings, benchmark) are undated, so the captions are the only evidence for the footings and the benchmark. Staffing after 1965 is not in these sources. The 'How footings disappear' caption is quoted only as evidence of footings. One WebSearch used; it found nothing new on the site today.
